item.title: Kodiak to launch driverless IKEA freight on Texas I-45 later this year
item.description:
Kodiak AI will haul IKEA freight with no one in the cab on a 219-mile stretch of Interstate 45 in Texas later this year. IKEA Supply is the launch shipper for the service, which forms part of an existing 292-mile route between its Baytown distribution center and Frisco store.
The driverless trips mainly operate between Kodiak’s facilities in Houston and the Dallas area. In the last four years, Kodiak moved over 1,300 IKEA loads autonomously with a safety observer, covering more than 750,000 miles. Starting in August, Kodiak launched its driverless long-haul program and now regularly hauls freight between its Lancaster, Texas hub and Houston without anyone behind the wheel. Kodiak’s autonomy readiness measure was 93% at the end of August, up from 84% in February, and the company expects to reach 100% and launch driverless operations by year-end.
“Unsupervised driverless operations – no human in the cab – represent a milestone the entire Kodiak team has been tirelessly working toward since Kodiak was founded more than eight years ago,” Don Burnette, founder and CEO, Kodiak AI said.
“They can reduce their time sleeping on the side of the highway and instead be home with family and friends,” Don Burnette, founder and CEO, Kodiak AI said.
Over the past four years, Kodiak has delivered more than 1,300 loads and logged more than 750,000 miles carrying IKEA goods autonomously with a safety observer aboard, founder and CEO Don Burnette wrote in a company post announcing the partnership update. The company began its driverless long-haul launch program in August and said it now consistently completes deliveries between its Lancaster, Texas, hub and Houston without human intervention. Kodiak already runs driverless trucks commercially for Atlas Energy Solutions in the Permian Basin, work that began in December 2024.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/kodiak-ikea-driverless-freight-i-45)

item.title: Happy Returns integrates with TikTok Shop to offer box‑free returns
item.description:
Happy Returns announced on Tuesday that its reverse‑logistics platform is now integrated into TikTok Shop, providing shoppers a box‑free, label‑free return option. The integration targets a market where TikTok Shop logged over 103 billion searches in the U.S. in 2025 and where mail‑in returns are six times more prone to fraud than in‑person drops.
Shoppers can start a return in the TikTok app and drop off items at any of Happy Returns’ Return Bar locations nationwide, receiving an instant refund without needing a box or a label. The option is available to participating retailers whether they fulfill orders themselves or rely on TikTok Shop’s fulfillment service. Happy Returns already processes returns for brands such as Everlane, Allbirds, Shein, Fabletics, Revolve and Under Armour.
“Our TikTok Shop partnership brings Happy Returns into one of the fastest-growing commerce ecosystems, giving greater confidence at purchase while supporting the fraud-resistant, scalable returns infrastructure merchants need to grow,” David Sobie, co‑founder and CEO of Happy Returns said.
“Our collaboration with Happy Returns builds on our commitment to making the returns experience faster, hassle‑free, and more trustworthy for our shoppers, with box‑free, label‑free returns and instant refunds at approximately 10,000 Return Bar locations nationwide,” Patrick Nommensen, president of strategic initiatives at TikTok Shop said.
Happy Returns already handles returns for brands including Everlane, Allbirds, Shein, Fabletics, Revolve and Under Armour.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/happy-returns-is-now-intergrates-into-tiktok-1239287966)

item.title: Airbus completes first test flight of A350 freighter, targets late-2027 delivery
item.description:
Airbus completed the first test flight of its A350 widebody freighter on Tuesday, reaching 25,000 feet and flying for four hours and ten minutes. The manufacturer has tallied 103 orders from 14 customers and expects the first commercial delivery in late 2027.
The freighter offers a payload of 111 metric tons and features the industry's widest cargo door at 175 inches.
“We can say it has been built by Airbus, but really it has been designed by the market. The market was sending us a very strong signal. Operators were coming to us to say they wanted choice. They didn’t want just one option in terms of what they could buy for a large freighter,” Sarah McLaren, head of widebody and freighter marketing said.
Airbus began designing the A350 freighter last decade, basing it on the successful A350-1000 passenger aircraft. The freighter is intended to be Airbus’s first production aircraft capable of challenging Boeing’s dominance in the cargo market.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/airbus-a350-freighter-aircraft-completes-initial-test-flight)

item.title: Panama Canal Authority raises daily Neopanamax transits to 10 starting Oct. 15
item.description:
The Panama Canal Authority will increase daily Neopanamax lock transits to 10 beginning Oct. 15, lifting total daily capacity across the Neopanamax and Panamax locks to 33 slots. It also restored the maximum authorized draft for Neopanamax vessels to 49 feet, letting ships carry more cargo through the canal.
Before the change, the Authority had cut daily transit capacity to as few as 32 ships in mid-September and imposed draft limits as Gatun Lake fell during a prolonged water shortage. The new allocation brings combined Neopanamax and Panamax lock capacity to 33 slots per day, the highest level since the drought‑related restrictions began. A 10,000‑TEU containership loses about 450 TEUs of capacity for each foot of draft restriction, so the deeper draft can recover hundreds of slots of cargo per vessel.
Earlier in the year, the Authority reduced daily transit capacity and imposed draft limits after a prolonged water shortage lowered Gatun Lake, the principal reservoir supplying the locks. Near‑average rainfall and water‑conservation measures at the locks have since allowed the Authority to ease those restrictions.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/new-limits-more-ships-can-transit-this-key-cargo-chokepoint)

item.title: German security agencies move to block Cosco’s 80% stake bid for Zippel
item.description:
German security agencies are reportedly set to block Cosco’s bid to acquire an 80% stake in Hamburg logistics firm Konrad Zippel. The agencies warn the purchase would form part of a broader Chinese strategy to gain a foothold at Hamburg’s port, despite Zippel’s modest 1.5% share of the local freight‑forwarding market.
Under Cosco’s proposal, the state‑owned Chinese shipping giant would take an 80% stake through its Dutch subsidiary Goldlead Supply Chain Development, leaving founder Axel Plass with the remaining 20%. The deal had already cleared Germany’s antitrust authority, Bundeskartellamt, back in February. Plass has insisted the transaction is about winning and retaining cargo and that all jobs would be preserved. The security agencies’ objection stems not from the stake itself but from its addition to Cosco’s existing 24.99% holding in the Tollerot container terminal, which they view as a cumulative acquisition strategy.
“all jobs will be preserved,” Axel Plass, MD said.
Earlier this year, Cosco secured a 24.99% stake in Hamburg’s Tollerot container terminal after a six‑month security review, following an initial attempt to take a 35% share that was blocked by German authorities. The current bid for Zippel would add to that holding, prompting security agencies to warn of a cumulative acquisition strategy. Zippel’s managing director has repeatedly said the transaction is aimed at preserving jobs and winning cargo, not at strategic control.
Source: The Loadstar (https://theloadstar.com/german-security-agencies-baulk-at-cosco-bid-for-zippel)

item.title: Hapag-Lloyd raises 2026 profit outlook by over $1bn after strong peak season
item.description:
Hapag-Lloyd raised its 2026 profit outlook by more than $1bn after a strong, elongated container shipping peak season this year, according to an investor note yesterday. The company upgraded its full-year EBITDA guidance to a range of $3.9bn to $4.4bn, up from the previous $2.7bn-$3.7bn forecast.
The upward revision adds over $1bn to Hapag-Lloyd's projected earnings for 2026. The strong, elongated container shipping peak season this year drove the earnings increase. The investor note that disclosed the upgrade was published yesterday.
Gemini Cooperation partners Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd plan to reroute their Asia-Med Loop 1 next month. Gemini's second Asia-Med service has returned to the Suez route as CMA attempts to prop up rates.
Source: The Loadstar (https://theloadstar.com/hapag-lloyd-ups-2026-profit-forecast-and-submits-revised-zim-bid)

item.title: Delegates hear air cargo must connect fragmented data across supply chain
item.description:
Delegates at Aviation Connect in Athens heard today that air cargo’s next digital challenge is connecting fragmented data across the supply chain, not merely digitising more processes. Accenture Cargo’s product growth lead Shanmugam Thangavelu said changing trade patterns, growing capacity and the emergence of AI are pushing the industry toward better data integration. He also noted that advance booking is critical as hi-tech solutions capture peak airfreight capacity during the current season.
The briefing highlighted that data silos between booking platforms, customs authorities, ground handlers and last‑mile carriers hinder real‑time visibility. AI tools can ingest disparate feeds to predict demand spikes and optimise cargo routing, reducing the need for last‑minute charter flights. Delegates heard that integrating these data streams could cut average transit times by up to 15% during peak periods.
Source: The Loadstar (https://theloadstar.com/bridging-the-gaps-in-air-cargo-data-an-ideal-challenge-for-ai)

item.title: Not On The High Street raises TV/VOD spend 120% for festive campaign
item.description:
Not On The High Street launched a two-part Autumn and Christmas campaign on October 1, boosting its TV and VOD investment by 120% compared with last year. The campaign features a 30‑second brand film airing from October 1 and a 45‑second Christmas spot running from November through mid‑December.
The films were directed by Benji Jackson and Will Warr of Detail Films, with Warr also known for filming Princess Kate’s ‘Mother Nature’ series. Real artisans Kate Brigden, Posh Totty and This is Nessie appear in the Autumn film, while the Christmas spot’s hero prop was handcrafted by Welsh partner MijMoj. NOTHS said the increased spend aims to capture early festive shoppers and build sustained emotional brand affinity during the peak Q4 period, when partners generate about 44% of their yearly sales.
“This year, we wanted to return to the very heart of what makes Not On The High Street so special. That meant doubling down on what has always set us apart: the incredible talent and individuality of our small business community, the real people behind every product, and the deeply emotional connections that thoughtful gifting can create,” Rachel Wells, VP Brand & Experience at Not On The High Street said.
Last year NOTHS ran a shorter festive TV/VOD push with lower investment; this year's campaign marks a 120% increase over that spend.
Source: ChannelX (https://channelx.world/2026/09/not-on-the-high-street-doubles-tv-investment-with-autumn-and-christmas-campaigns)

item.title: Aldi boss accuses rivals of duping shoppers with loyalty prices
item.description:
Aldi UK boss Giles Hurley accused rival supermarkets of duping shoppers with loyalty prices as Aldi reported group sales across the UK and Ireland rose five per cent to a record £19bn in 2025. Operating profit edged down to £432.9m as the retailer absorbed higher wage bills and continued investing in prices, stores and infrastructure.
Aldi said it has invested £340m in price cuts this year to reinforce its value credentials amid intense competition across the grocery sector. The retailer is committing £900m to its UK business in 2027, which will fund 40 new supermarkets and further spending on its distribution network as it works toward a long‑term target of 1,500 UK stores. It currently operates 1,092 stores and is preparing to open 30 new locations in the coming weeks. The Competition and Markets Authority analysed around 50,000 loyalty‑priced products across Tesco, Sainsbury’s, Waitrose, Co‑op and Morrisons and found that 92 per cent offered a genuine saving, with shoppers typically saving between 17 per cent and 25 per cent.
“However, when promotions start with unrealistically high prices and come down to prices which aren’t that competitive and dupe customers, we would view that as loyalty that isn’t supportive, that isn’t transparent and doesn’t help customers plan and budget,” Giles Hurley, Aldi UK boss said.
Aldi remains the only major UK supermarket without a loyalty scheme, and Hurley’s comments come despite a Competition and Markets Authority investigation that found little evidence of routine price inflation for loyalty discounts. The watchdog’s analysis of around 50,000 loyalty‑priced products showed 92% offered genuine savings, though it warned loyalty prices were not always the cheapest across the market.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/aldi-boss-accuses-rivals-of-duping-shoppers-with-loyalty-prices)

item.title: Ex-eBay Manager Sues Over Alleged Seller Favoritism, 2012 Acquisition Metrics
item.description:
Former eBay Motors Manager Anson Tse sued eBay on September 25, alleging seller favoritism and saying the Parts & Accessories business delivered 21% year‑over‑year growth in 2012. The Administrative Review Board affirmed the earlier dismissal of his claims on August 31, 2026, prompting Tse to seek de novo review in federal court.
Tse worked for eBay from 2007 to 2015, starting as Manager, Enthusiast Vehicles and later serving as interim head of the Parts & Accessories business.
“before the Secretary of Labor issued a final decision,” Anson Tse, former eBay Motors Manager said.
Tse first filed a Sarbanes‑Oxley whistleblower complaint with OSHA in 2015, which OSHA dismissed, and a Department of Labor Administrative Law Judge later denied his claims after a six‑day hearing. The Administrative Review Board affirmed that decision on August 31, 2026, but Tse is now seeking de novo review in federal court under a SOX provision that allows exit when the Labor Department fails to issue a final decision within 180 days.
Source: Value Added Resource (https://valueaddedresource.net/ex-ebay-whistleblower-new-lawsuit)

item.title: Diesel up 10 cents, spot rates up 2 cents, squeezing trucking margins
item.description:
Diesel prices rose $0.10 per gallon in one week to just under $6.57 while truckload spot rates gained only $0.02 per mile over the same period, according to FreightWaves data as of Monday, Sept. 28. The widening gap between fuel costs and spot rates is compressing margins for trucking companies and putting a premium on load utilization.
The National Truckload Index was 5.2% higher than a month earlier, when it stood at $3.28 per mile, while diesel prices were 16.5% above the same prior month. Tender rejections have remained near 14%, a level described as healthy and well above year‑ago readings, giving carriers continued negotiating leverage with shippers. Regulatory pressure on non‑domiciled commercial driver’s licenses and the shutdown of substandard driving schools are raising barriers to entry, further tightening capacity independent of demand. Freight demand remains muted as the Sonar Truckload Volume Index has stayed flat through 2024, with weak automotive and housing sectors keeping overall volumes low heading into peak season. Contract rates continue to climb, intermodal maintains momentum as shippers convert loads for cost savings, and inbound import volumes remain solid.
“Fuel is rising more quickly than spot rates,” Julie Van de Kamp, analyst said.
“There are so many reasons that there’s still pressure on trucking companies and pulling demand capacity out of the market while demand has remained weak,” Julie Van de Kamp, analyst said.
Looking ahead through peak, Van de Kamp projected “an elongated and stable peak” rather than a sharp seasonal surge, with contract rates continuing to climb, intermodal maintaining momentum as shippers convert loads for cost savings, and inbound import volumes remaining solid. The Sonar Truckload Volume Index has held relatively flat through 2024, with two key freight drivers — automotive and housing — still running soft.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/diesel-up-10-cents-spot-rates-up-2-margin-squeeze)

item.title: Suez return cuts India-Savannah transit by 10-14 days
item.description:
Carriers including Maersk and CMA CGM have resumed Suez Canal routings for India-Savannah container services, cutting transit times by 10 to 14 days. Maersk’s MECL service now reaches Savannah in 28 days from Nhava Sheva, while CMA CGM’s Indamex service is expected to save five days on the same route. The Maersk Denver made the first westbound Suez transit for the service when it called Savannah on August 9.
The shift back through Suez avoids the longer Cape of Good Hope detour that had added distance, time and vessel capacity requirements. Mediterranean Shipping Co. plans to restore Suez routings on four Asia-Europe and Mediterranean services, allowing each to run with two fewer vessels. The Port of Savannah handles about 40 weekly vessel calls, 42 double-stack rail departures and nearly 15,000 truck moves each day.
“Georgia Ports welcomes the transit time improvements as several major carriers return to Suez routings linking Georgia to world markets,” Kevin Price, Georgia Ports President said.
“We are glad to see ocean carriers resuming Red Sea transits using the Suez Canal, the fastest and most economical way to link Asia, South and Southeast Asia and the Middle East to the U.S. market,” Flavio Batista, chief commercial officer at Georgia Ports Authority said.
Many container services had been diverted around Africa due to security risks in the Red Sea region. The Cape of Good Hope detour added considerable distance, time and vessel capacity requirements to several trade lanes.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/suez-return-speeds-up-savannah-india-service-by-10-14-days)

item.title: Netstock report shows over 2,500 SMBs juggling multiple supply chain risks
item.description:
Netstock surveyed more than 2,500 global SMBs for its 2026 Benchmark Report, finding they now juggle supplier volatility, raw material cost fluctuations, and demand shifts instead of preparing for a single disruption. The report found that typical SMBs now turn inventory four times per year, the highest level in three years, while top performers average nearly eight turns annually.
The proportion of SMBs reporting more than 10% of inventory as dead stock has doubled since 2024. The share of SMBs saying they do not use AI or are unsure of its effectiveness has been cut in half since 2024. Concerns about data integrity and security in AI applications have risen from 23% of respondents in 2024 to 39% this year. Supplier lead-time swings were cited by 29% of respondents as a planning challenge.
“Businesses are no longer preparing for a single disruption,” Ara Ohanian, CEO of Netstock said.
Since 2024, the portion of SMBs reporting they do not use AI or are uncertain about its effectiveness has fallen by half. At the same time, worries over data integrity and security in AI have grown from 23% to 39% of respondents, and the share of SMBs with over 10% dead stock has doubled.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/supply-chain-report-reveals-challenges-facing-smbs-netstock-1239283943)

item.title: Shopify adds category metafields to Analytics for filtering and grouping reports
item.description:
Shopify now makes category metafields available as dimensions and filters in its Analytics tool. Merchants whose products already have category metafields can use them immediately without any additional configuration.
Users can group sales reports by Color. Users can group sales reports by Material. Users can group sales reports by Fit. Users can group sales reports by Fabric. Users can group sales reports by Size. Users can group sales reports by Activity. Users can group sales reports by any other category metafield they have defined. Merchants can filter reports to a specific value such as organic cotton. Merchants can filter reports to a particular color. The metafields can be applied in Reports. The metafields can be applied in Explore. The metafields can be applied in the query editor. The process of categorizing products has not changed. Existing custom metafields continue to work exactly as before. When a product has multiple values for an attribute, Analytics combines them on a single row to avoid double‑counting sales.
Until now, the color, material, fit, and other attributes you set when you categorize a product stayed on the product page. To see which materials or colors actually sell, you had to export.
Source: Shopify Changelog (https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/category-metafields-are-now-available-in-analytics)

item.title: Retailers expect U.S. holiday e‑commerce sales to reach $275.1 billion in 2026
item.description:
Adobe projects that U.S. online sales for the 2026 holiday season (Nov. 1–Dec. 31) will rise 6.7% year over year to $275.1 billion. For Cyber Week, the five‑day span between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday, Adobe forecasts online sales of $47.5 billion, a 7.4% increase, with Cyber Monday alone topping $15 billion, up 6.2%. Black Friday is expected to generate $12.9 billion, a 9.2% jump, making it the second‑largest single‑day holiday spend after Cyber Monday.
Adobe predicts that during Cyber Week, personal‑hygiene product sales will surge 150% versus September averages, clothing basics 210%, baby products 113%, pet items 93% and household cleaners 49%. The season’s top categories are electronics at $63.3 billion (+5.9%) and apparel at $51.3 billion (+4.7%), while furniture reaches $33.4 billion (+7.3%) and grocery, toys and cosmetics each near $26.1 billion, $9.6 billion and $9.2 billion respectively, all up about 10%. October’s Prime Big Deal Days are forecast to deliver almost $10 billion in online sales, pushing total October e‑commerce to $95.8 billion, an 8% year‑over‑year gain, while average discount depths stay flat versus 2025. Thanksgiving Day sales are seen at $6.9 billion (+8.5%) with 63% of orders on mobile, up from 61.6% in 2025, and mobile drives 82% of buy‑now‑pay‑later usage, lifting holiday BNPL to $21.3 billion (+6.6%) and AI‑driven site traffic to jump 130%.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/holiday-season-ecommerce-sales-growth-2026/831121)

item.title: Hy-Vee rebrands all 22 Dollar Fresh Market stores as Hy-Vee
item.description:
Hy-Vee announced it is converting all 22 of its Dollar Fresh Market locations into standard Hy-Vee stores, a shift disclosed by CEO Jeremy Gosch at the Groceryshop keynote on Thursday. The decision follows a January announcement to rebrand four of the stores, which the chain is now extending to the full Dollar Fresh portfolio.
Hy-Vee launched the Dollar Fresh Market format in 2018 as a low‑price banner aimed at competing with dollar retailers. As part of the conversion, each store is receiving an expanded assortment that grew by several thousand items in the first four pilot locations. The remodeled stores also gain bakeries, service meat cases, a health market and a prepared‑foods section offering sandwiches, salads and pizzas. Hy-Vee said the changes reflect what customers have come to expect from its brand, even in more remote locations.
“We tried Dollar Fresh Market — a different brand, low-price operator going for real rural small towns. And what we found is a 96-year-old brand has got way more staying power in any market than trying to have a startup with a different name, because you’re known for something and that’s what you have to hang your hat on,” Jeremy Gosch, CEO said.
Hy-Vee’s Dollar Fresh Markets, which launched in 2018, were the regional grocer’s attempt to take on dollar retailers. The grocer had made transitions like this before, he noted, pointing to Hy-Vee’s decision to convert all of its Wahlburgers restaurants into Market Grille locations in early 2025.
Source: Grocery Dive (https://grocerydive.com/news/hy-vee-dollar-fresh-market-transition-groceryshop/831402)

item.title: Amazon leads ecommerce marketplaces in AI visibility with 19.3% share of voice
item.description:
Amazon leads top ecommerce marketplaces in AI visibility with a 19.3% share of voice, according to new analysis from Onclusive. Walmart followed with 14% share of voice, while Amazon also scored the highest prominence at 92% versus Walmart’s 84%. Amazon garnered 16.4 million media mentions, far above Walmart’s 5.6 million, and NIQ research shows 74% of global shoppers now use AI for product discovery.
The study measured share of voice by counting how often each marketplace appeared in responses from ChatGPT and Perplexity.
“What stands out from this analysis is how quickly a new hierarchy of brand visibility is forming within generative AI. The major marketplaces are not appearing equally, and the gap between the most and least visible brands is already significant,” Christophe Asselin, Senior Insights Manager at Onclusive said.
Generative AI now forms another layer of brand discovery alongside traditional search, social media and other digital channels.
Source: ChannelX (https://channelx.world/2026/09/amazon-leads-ecommerce-marketplaces-for-ai-visibility)

item.title: Avalara launches Aviator hub to cut tax work from days to minutes
item.description:
Avalara launched its Aviator agent hub, built on more than 22 years of compliance data, at the CRUSH customer and partner conference. The hub uses AI agents to turn days of manual compliance work into minutes of oversight.
Avalara says the Aviator hub is initially available to existing customers at no extra charge. Its orchestrator AI, Avi, can draft tax rules, simulate impacts, and flag conflicts before activation. Capabilities include mapping products to tax codes, reporting liability data, validating exemption certificates, generating tax matrices, analyzing results, and configuring custom rules. Over time, Avalara plans to extend the agentic capabilities into ERP, e‑commerce, finance and collaboration platforms already used by customers.
“Our customers need a system they can trust to get real work done. Avalara Aviator fulfills that need,” Hugo Sarrazin, Chief Executive Officer at Avalara said.
Previously, tax software handled individual tasks such as calculations and filings, while the steps between them remained manual and isolated. As companies expand across more markets and channels, tax rules have become more interconnected, digital, and real‑time.
Source: ChannelX (https://channelx.world/2026/09/avalara-aviator-hub-launched-for-ai-agents-moving-from-answers-to-execution)

item.title: Iceland Foods deploys AI platform to cut food waste across stores
item.description:
Iceland Foods has announced it will deploy Retail Insight’s WasteInsight AI platform to reduce food waste across its store estate. The platform analyses operational data to flag products nearing expiry and recommends margin‑protective markdowns so staff can act before waste occurs.
The software prioritises items that need attention and suggests specific actions based on a range of operational data points. By providing these prompts, the system aims to standardise markdown decisions across all Iceland stores, moving away from reliance on manual checks or retrospective reports. The platform aims to enable store staff to act before waste occurs by stepping in earlier than manual checks or retrospective reports would allow. He said the opportunity lies in shifting from reporting past events to pinpointing where action is needed before waste occurs. He added that the retailer is continually seeking ways to use operational data to help colleagues make faster, better‑informed decisions in stores. He also noted that working with Retail Insight will help explore how AI‑driven operational intelligence can support waste‑reduction objectives while improving consistency across store operations.
“Retailers have access to more operational data than ever before, but data only creates value when it enables better decisions,” Martin Rigby, Retail Insight general manager for EMEA and APAC said.
“an important priority,” Steve Shirley, Iceland Foods stores director said.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/iceland-taps-ai-to-cut-food-waste-across-stores)

item.title: Stagwell’s AI chief outlines Palantir‑based platform for brand customers
item.description:
Stagwell announced last November a partnership with Palantir to develop an AI‑driven data and audience platform for its Marketing Cloud. John Kahan, who brings four decades of data and analytics experience from IBM and Microsoft, was named chief AI officer and interim CEO of the Marketing Cloud to lead the initiative.
The platform is designed to be cloud‑ and model‑agnostic, allowing Stagwell’s customers to run any large language model on any infrastructure they choose. It can ingest structured and unstructured data from disparate sources, use an LLM to make sense of it, and then deliver targeted ads that align with both consumer demand and the brand’s supply‑chain capabilities. By testing models in real‑world scenarios and deploying sovereign models built on open‑weight Nvidia chips, Stagwell says it can lower costs, protect customer data, and avoid vendor lock‑in for advertisers. The system also enables brands to hook the platform directly into their supply‑chain software, allowing real‑time adjustments to media spend based on inventory levels and financial performance.
“With Palantir I can test any model against another model, real time in a real world scenario, and put the best model at the right cost factor for our customers directly in their hands,” John Kahan, chief AI officer and interim CEO of Stagwell’s Marketing Cloud said.
Prior to the partnership, Stagwell’s deal with Palantir drew skepticism because the defense‑focused firm was not an obvious fit for a marketing holding company. CEO Mark Penn had previously known Palantir’s CEO Alex Karp and believed the firm’s capabilities could give Stagwell an edge over larger rivals. Since the announcement, Elspeth Rollert has resumed leadership of the Marketing Cloud after returning from maternity leave.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media-buying/media-buying-briefing-stagwells-chief-ai-officer-explains-why-palantir-differentiates-its-data-platform-from-competitors)

item.title: Industry leaders pause entry-level hiring as AI reshapes workforce
item.description:
At Digiday Media’s AI Marketing Strategies event on Sept. 24, industry leaders said they have paused hiring entry-level talent, citing AI’s takeover of tasks once handled by workers aged 18-34. They also noted that a Pew Research survey found workers aged 18-34 are more concerned about AI‑related job loss than older cohorts.
Executives explained that AI tools now perform many of the routine duties that previously fell to recent college graduates, such as data entry, basic ad‑trafficking and preliminary analytics. One participant, the owner of a small‑to‑mid‑sized performance marketing agency, said the firm used to hire entry‑level talent exclusively and that many of those hires became top performers. Another attendee warned that cutting graduate hiring is short‑sighted because agencies will lose institutional knowledge when senior staff retire, and urged companies to redesign junior roles rather than eliminate them. The group agreed on solutions that include formal mentorship programs, AI‑training courses for current employees, and internships that pay livable wages to attract and develop new talent.
“We haven’t hired college-level grads in some time, and I don’t anticipate that we will be,” Owner of a small-to-mid-sized performance marketing agency said.
The discussion took place under Chatham House Rules, which granted participants anonymity to speak candidly about workforce trends. Prior to the event, executives across advertising and marketing had already linked rapid AI adoption to a growing talent crisis, noting inconsistencies in how the technology is being applied.
Source: Modern Retail (https://modernretail.co/retailers/not-hiring-entry-level-talent-industry-acknowledges-runaway-crisis-brought-on-by-introducing-ai-to-the-workforce)

item.title: Burton marks 50 years, eyes streetwear and China growth
item.description:
Burton marks its 50th anniversary as it looks to expand into streetwear and China. The company cites China’s winter sports economy, now worth nearly $150 billion, as a key growth driver.
Denny Bruce became CEO on September 21 after serving as a regional manager at Burton and holding roles at Vans and Dickies. In 2023 Burton generated over $350 million in sales, though it does not disclose full financials. Burton plans to grow its year‑round lifestyle apparel, launching a capsule collection called Zeb’s Closet with pro snowboarder Zeb Powell.
“One of our great competitive advantages is we’re privately held,” Donna Carpenter, owner and chair of Burton’s board said.
“China also has a much larger ratio of snowboarders to skiers, at about 75% to 25%,” Donna Carpenter, owner and chair of Burton’s board said.
John Lacy stepped down as CEO in June, leading Donna Carpenter to serve as interim CEO. Burton launched a new flagship store in Manhattan as part of its broader transformation. Before Denny Bruce’s appointment, Carpenter led the company on an interim basis while the search for a permanent CEO continued.
Source: Glossy (https://glossy.co/fashion/burton-at-50-the-snowboard-icon-is-setting-its-sights-on-streetwear-and-china)

item.title: Unilever Wellbeing reports seven wellness brands after Olly acquisition
item.description:
Unilever Wellbeing now owns seven wellness-oriented brands, following its 2019 acquisition of Olly. Four of those brands are designated power brands, namely Olly, Liquid I.V., Nutrafol and Grü.
Solheim said that ten years ago beauty was defined mainly by appearance, but consumers have moved from dieting for looks to dieting for health and now to a combined wellness‑beauty approach. He outlined three shifts: first, health goals aimed at weight management and disease prevention; second, the convergence of beauty and well‑being; third, the digitalization that puts science and data in the hands of consumers. Solheim added that GLP‑1 drugs and AI‑assisted health data are giant accelerators, encouraging a more proactive stance on personal health. Solheim noted that consumers have increasingly taken agency over their own health and integrated wellness into everyday life, which gave an opportunity for branding and building deeper relationships.
“Four [are] what we at Unilever call power brands,” Jostein Solheim, CEO of Unilever Wellbeing said.
“[It was] the original disruptor of the vitamin shelf,” Jostein Solheim, CEO of Unilever Wellbeing said.
Historically, Unilever was known primarily as one of the world's largest food companies, but it has since reshaped its portfolio to blend food, beverage and better-for-you wellness brands. In 2019 it bought Olly to expand its vitamin and supplement line, marking the start of its wellness‑focused brand building. The move came as the company observed shifting consumer priorities toward health‑linked beauty products.
Source: Modern Retail (https://modernretail.co/operations/how-unilever-sees-the-line-between-beauty-and-wellness-blurring)

item.title: Amazon to invest $3 billion in India quick commerce by 2030
item.description:
Amazon will invest $3 billion to expand its India quick-commerce business by 2030, according to two sources. The investment will be split, with $1 billion earmarked by end-2027 and a further $2 billion by 2030. Amazon's quick-commerce arm already generates over $1 billion in annualised gross sales.
The company plans to grow its Amazon Now network from about 750 neighbourhood warehouses to roughly 1,300 by April 2027. Amazon holds a 6.2% share of India's quick-commerce market, while rivals Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto together control 77% and Flipkart 11%. The broader quick-commerce sector was valued at $19 billion and is forecast to exceed $41 billion by 2030, according to Datum Intelligence. Investment will also fund upgraded inventory-management software, AI-driven demand forecasting and a broader selection of daily essentials, excluding items such as smartphones.
Walmart's Flipkart and Amazon, despite dominating India's overall e-commerce market, entered the quick-commerce space later than rivals. As the sector grew after 2022, safety concerns rose over delivery bikers speeding through neighbourhoods, prompting the Indian government in January to ban advertising of ten-minute delivery times.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/09/28/what-will-amazons-3-billion-quick-commerce-bet-buy)

item.title: Tesla opens Nevada Semi factory, cites April start and 50k‑truck yearly capacity
item.description:
Tesla opened its 1.7‑million‑square‑foot Semi factory in Sparks, Nevada on September 24. The facility is designed to produce up to 50,000 trucks each year. The first Semi rolled off the line in April, months before the inauguration event.
Deliveries of the Semi have gone to customers including DHL, PepsiCo, and US Foods. The plant sits next to Gigafactory Nevada, allowing the Semi to use Tesla’s in‑house 4680 battery cells produced on site. Tesla said the Semi now consumes about 1.6 to 1.7 kilowatt‑hours per mile, roughly 25 % better than its original 2,000‑watt‑hour‑per‑mile target. A pilot fleet of just under 200 trucks accumulated about 17.5 million miles, and regenerative braking handles most deceleration, reducing brake wear.
The Semi idea originated in 2014 when Tesla noted its battery parts were being shipped on diesel trucks. Design work moved from modeling to hardware in early 2016, and two alpha trucks were shown publicly in 2017. A pilot fleet of just under 200 trucks entered service in 2022, logging roughly 17.5 million miles before full production began.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/tesla-marked-the-start-of-high-volume-semi-production-and-the-engineering-story-sits-underneath-the-cab)

item.title: Hapag‑Lloyd revises $4.2 billion Zim offer to address Israeli security concerns
item.description:
Hapag‑Lloyd and FIMI submitted a revised takeover proposal for Zim Integrated Shipping Services on September 24, valuing the Israeli carrier at $4.2 billion. The offer maintains the $35‑per‑share cash price while proposing to lower the foreign‑ownership trigger for the Israeli successor from 24% to 10%.
Under the revised structure, Hapag‑Lloyd would take control of Zim’s international liner business, while FIMI would create a separate Israeli company, Zim Israel, to hold assets protected by Israel’s ‘golden share’ provisions. The proposal calls for the Israeli entity to receive 16 vessels, be debt‑free, and make those ships available to the government during emergencies while maintaining maritime links. Hapag‑Lloyd said the changes are intended to further strengthen Israel’s maritime security and independence and to secure Israeli access to key shipping routes from Asia. Hapag‑Lloyd noted that the combined entity would operate more than 400 vessels, exceed three million TEUs of capacity and move over 18 million TEUs annually, though it would remain the world’s seventh‑largest container carrier.
The original deal, announced in February, had Hapag‑Lloyd acquiring Zim for $35 per share in cash, a 58% premium to the February 13 share price. Zim’s shareholders approved the transaction, but it has awaited clearance from Israeli ministries overseeing defense, ports and state‑owned companies. Israel’s golden‑share provisions are designed to preserve the state’s ability to ensure maritime service during emergencies and maintain control over designated strategic shipping capabilities.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/hapag-lloyd-revises-zim-offer-as-israeli-approval-concerns-persist)

item.title: Mud Jeans returns under new owners after 255,000‑euro sale
item.description:
Mud Jeans was sold to Horizon Capital and N5 Holding for 255,000 euros after filing for bankruptcy in August. Nick de Ronde Bresser will lead the company as CEO while founder Bert van Son returns to oversee brand experience and circularity.
quotes
“I think it’s great that we can continue this brand in Dutch hands and build a strong and healthy next phase together,” Nick de Ronde Bresser, who will serve as Mud Jeans CEO said.
“The bankruptcy was painful, but Mud’s mission is alive and well. I am happy to be back and to be able to build a healthier company together with the new owners,” Bert van Son, founder said.
Mud Jeans was founded in 2012 and became known for pioneering recycled‑cotton jeans and take‑back programs, but a heavy debt load and weak demand led to an August bankruptcy filing.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sj-denim/mud-jeans-new-owners-n5-bert-van-son-1239260002)

item.title: Marketers say AI ad standards are slipping
item.description:
Marketers at the inaugural AI Marketing Strategies event on Sept. 24 discussed automated workflows and AI-driven job cuts as companies considered higher content output while trying to preserve brand standards across digital supply chains. One participant treated AI-generated creative as a rough draft under a 10/80/10 formula: 10% for prompting, 80% for the middle work and 10% for getting good work. Participants said agency partners often rely on junior employees to oversee AI platforms, while one brand-side participant said they had to insist on human oversight before campaign executions were allowed to run.
Marketers at the inaugural AI Marketing Strategies event on Sept. 24 discussed automated workflows and AI-driven job cuts as companies considered higher content output while trying to preserve brand standards across digital supply chains. One participant treated AI-generated creative as a rough draft under a 10/80/10 formula: 10% for prompting, 80% for the middle work and 10% for getting good work. Participants said agency partners often rely on junior employees to oversee AI platforms, while one brand-side participant said they had to insist on human oversight before campaign executions were allowed to run.
Early AI-era pitches centered on innovation and efficiency, but the coverage says mounting ad-industry job losses and a resulting decline in standards have created weariness. Marketers and advertising teams are seeking new standards and a talent base fit for contemporary challenges. The town hall was held under Chatham House Rules, and the event was co-hosted by Digiday and its sister titles Glossy and Modern Retail.
Source: Modern Retail (https://modernretail.co/technology/marketers-bemoan-the-culture-of-good-enough-go-as-standards-fall-amid-the-ai-bubble)

item.title: SMBs expand multi‑region sourcing to 55% as China lead‑time worries rise
item.description:
Small and midsize businesses are expanding their supplier base across more regions and ordering earlier, according to Netstock’s 2026 survey of over 2,500 customers worldwide. The share of SMBs sourcing from at least two of the four tracked regions rose to 55% in 2026, up from 45% in 2024.
When allowed to cite multiple pressures, supplier timing appeared among the top three concerns for 77% of SMBs, freight and shipping for 72%, raw materials and input costs for 66%, and demand shifts for 57%. Supplier lead-time swings ranked as the top inventory planning challenge for 29% of respondents, while raw material and input costs, freight and shipping costs, and demand shifts followed at 23%, 22% and 21% respectively. In 2025, 61% of SMBs sourcing from China cited long supplier lead times, compared with 52% of businesses elsewhere; this year those figures rose to 75% and 42%, widening the China sourcing gap from 9 to 33 percentage points. Preference for offshore sourcing fell to 21% in 2026 from 31% in 2024, while domestic sourcing preference increased to 23% over the same period, and only 35% of U.S. SMB respondents reported changing suppliers due to tariffs in the past year. Netstock also found that lead-time variability affects 74% of SMBs, long lead times affect 63%, and minimum order quantities affect 60%. The findings suggest freight demand could become increasingly fragmented as smaller businesses diversify suppliers, shift purchase orders between countries and adjust shipment timing rather than relying on the relatively straightforward inventory-building strategies that characterized 2025.
Last year, tariffs were a dominant concern and prompted businesses to front-load orders and build buffer inventories. In 2025, 61% of SMBs sourcing from China cited long supplier lead times, compared with 52% of businesses sourcing elsewhere.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/china-lead-time-concerns-surge-as-shippers-widen-global-sourcing-networks)

item.title: Square launches Apple Business integration for sellers in eight countries
item.description:
Square has launched an Apple Business integration that lets sellers manage their physical locations on Apple Maps and other Apple apps, offered in eight countries. Sellers in the United States and Canada who do not yet have an Apple Business account can enroll directly from the Square Dashboard.
Once connected, hours, addresses, and phone numbers updated in Square sync automatically to each location’s Apple Maps place card. Sellers can also add a logo and action buttons such as Order, Delivery, or Book that link to their Square ordering or booking pages. The integration is accessed through the Square Dashboard and builds on Square’s earlier AI partnerships with ChatGPT and Claude. Square says future updates may include place‑card engagement metrics and peer‑group benchmarks for merchants.
“This integration means our sellers don’t have to choose between running their business and keeping every channel updated,” Morgan Kuntze, global partnership lead at Square parent company Block said.
The new Apple Business integration comes after Square’s earlier AI tools that connect sellers with ChatGPT and Claude to help them appear in customer searches. Square has partnered with Amazon to bring its AI‑driven discovery to voice shoppers via Alexa+. When announcing those AI integrations, Kuntze said in a press release that modern commerce is moving at a sprint and Square is built to help sellers appear everywhere customers are going.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/square-lets-sellers-sync-hours-logos-and-order-and-booking-buttons-to-apple-maps-through-a-new-apple-business-integration)

item.title: Nuuly tops 500,000 subscribers as inventory expands to 33,000 items
item.description:
Nuuly, the rental service of Urban Outfitters Inc., reported over 500,000 active subscribers and grew its inventory to more than 33,000 items. The platform now carries clothing from more than 500 external brand partners, including Nike, Barbour and J. Crew.
Nuuly offers algorithm-driven sizing and a pause‑and‑cancel feature to simplify the subscriber experience. Behind the front end, the company manages reverse logistics, continuously receiving, cleaning, repairing and re‑shipping each garment. David Hayne, president of Nuuly and chief technology officer of URBN, said the service aims to give women an affordable way to refresh their wardrobes.
“There’s a tension there between the desire for newness and the desire for variety, and then what it costs,” David Hayne, president of Nuuly and chief technology officer of URBN said.
“At the end of the day, Nuuly is a platform that helps drive brand awareness,” David Hayne, president of Nuuly and chief technology officer of URBN said.
Urban Outfitters Inc. introduced Nuuly as a subscription rental option as consumers questioned the financial and environmental impact of constantly buying new clothing.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/how-smart-logistics-tech-is-scaling-rentals-nuuly-urbn-1239259328)

item.title: East Coast Asia-US container rates hold at $9,600
item.description:
Last week, East Coast Asia-US container spot rates held steady at about $9,600 per forty-foot equivalent unit while West Coast rates rose 4% to more than $8,100 per FEU. Despite the increase, trans-Pacific rates remain well below the September 2021 peak when Asia-West Coast prices topped $20,000 per FEU.
The elevated trans-Pacific rates reflect strong U.S.-bound demand, weather-related port congestion in the Far East and carriers managing capacity through blanked sailings. Asia to North Europe spot rates fell 15% last week to about $3,700 per FEU, while Asia-Mediterranean rates dropped 7% to roughly $3,900 per FEU after exceeding $7,000 in July. Carriers are also reducing capacity in anticipation of softer volumes during China’s Golden Week holiday and a broader demand easing expected after the peak season ends in October. A possible indefinite strike at German ports could add to the pressure on Asia-North Europe services. The Verdi labor union is voting on a job action that could begin as early as October, potentially worsening terminal congestion and constraining carrier capacity.
The divergence follows an unusually early east-west peak season that began in May and lifted container spot rates sharply through early July, according to analyst and SONAR data contributor Freightos (NASDAQ: CRGO). Freightos said that the current market is more comparable to the 2024 peak season, when Red Sea diversions constrained effective vessel capacity.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/but-no-pandemic-high-asia-us-container-rate-at-9600)

item.title: PETA protests H&M and COS shows over wool, citing abuse allegations
item.description:
On September 13, two PETA activists stormed the COS runway at New York Fashion Week, and on September 17, three PETA supporters did the same at H&M’s London Fashion Week show. The disruption led to the resignation of Steven Kolb, then chief executive and president of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, after two decades in the role. PETA says its campaign targets H&M Group’s use of NATIVA‑certified wool, which it claims is linked to animal abuse.
NATIVA, created by Chargeurs Luxury Materials, certifies wool sourced from farms in Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, North America, Uruguay and Argentina and employs blockchain to trace the fibre from farm to consumer. PETA alleges that an undercover investigation at a South African wool operation it says was NATIVA‑certified showed workers kicking sheep, striking them with shearing equipment and a piece of wood, dragging lambs by their legs and cutting animals during shearing. The organisation also reported finding a lamb with a maggot‑infested wound and a dead lamb during that investigation. H&M responded that animal welfare is “very important” to it and that no animal should be harmed to make its products.
“These protests highlight that every wool garment is a product of suffering,” Ingrid Newkirk, PETA founder said.
PETA says its current campaign is focused on H&M Group and the use of wool that it alleges is obtained through animal rights abuses. The charity’s campaign intensified after a PETA Asia undercover investigation at a South African wool operation that, according to PETA, was NATIVA‑certified and connected to H&M Group’s supply chain.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/peta-hm-cos-wool)

item.title: Tesco pilots virtual try-on for 1,500 F&F items at Sandhurst Extra store
item.description:
Tesco has launched a pilot of virtual try-on technology for 1,500 F&F clothing items at its Sandhurst Extra store. The trial is part of a broader refresh of the F&F offering that adds new changing rooms, a dedicated service hub and an expanded in‑store range, while Tesco also rolls out hundreds of extra styles online.
Shoppers can upload or take a photo of themselves on a digital screen and then select a digital model to see how garments look in different sizes. In addition to the virtual try‑on, the Sandhurst Extra store features updated lighting, new signage and a larger F&F selection across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear, plus clearer homeware displays. Online, Tesco has broadened its fashion catalogue with hundreds of additional styles, more size options and exclusive ranges, supported by improved search tools and curated styling inspiration.
Tesco first introduced its online fashion offer last year, which it described as successful, and is now expanding that digital assortment alongside the in‑store trial.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/tesco-trials-virtual-try-on)

item.title: Amazon adds eBay, Shopify, TikTok, Walmart links to Seller Central
item.description:
Amazon today launched multichannel selling tools in Seller Central that let sellers manage sales across Amazon, eBay, Shopify, TikTok and Walmart, a move aimed at the more than 95% of independent sellers who already sell on multiple channels, and the tools are free to use. The tools let sellers create and edit listings once, with changes automatically formatted for each channel’s requirements, view combined sales and profitability data, arrange fulfillment from Seller Central, and adjust pricing or inventory, manage returns, and track advertising performance, without leaving the dashboard.
Sellers easily start by visiting the multichannel settings page in Seller Central’s top‑right navigation bar, then click to connect their eBay, Shopify, TikTok or Walmart accounts. Connected data stays private and accessible only to the seller, who can import existing listings, link them to Amazon‑catalog products, and later disconnect any channel at will. Sellers can see combined order queues, print shipping labels, and track returns from a single dashboard, eliminating the need to log into each marketplace separately. The tools also sync inventory levels in real time, so a sale on one channel automatically reduces stock across all connected platforms, preventing overselling.
“We really believe that when sellers succeed across their entire business, they’re going to succeed on Amazon as well,” David Forsythe, Amazon’s VP of North America seller business said.
Amazon began its multichannel effort years ago after sellers said managing inventory across multiple places was a significant challenge. The company responded by launching Multichannel Fulfillment, Amazon Warehousing and Distribution, and Buy with Prime to create a unified inventory pool.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/small-business/amazon-seller-central-multichannel-selling-tools)

item.title: Amazon launches tools to cut global seller costs by up to 60%
item.description:
Amazon announced new tools that enable sellers to list a product once and sell in up to eight countries by year-end. Sellers active in more than one country earn 70% more revenue on average than those selling in just one.
The new compliance tools let sellers test a product once and receive certification valid in multiple countries, with early pilot participants reporting savings of up to 60%. Global Warehousing and Distribution will expand from the United States to eight countries by the end of the year, offering storage costs up to 45% lower than the existing U.S.-based Amazon Warehousing and Distribution service. A unified seller dashboard, introduced this fall, shows demand and economics across the United States, Europe and Japan, with additional countries to be added by year-end, and will eventually let sellers manage listings, inventory and orders in one place.
Amazon already reaches more rural U.S. shoppers than before, and it notes that only about three in ten sellers currently list products internationally. The company says the main hurdle is having to manage separate inventory, compliance, listings and logistics for each country.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-sellers-global-expansion-tools)

item.title: Lowe’s launches 20‑minute drone delivery in Matthews, NC with Wing and DoorDash
item.description:
Lowe’s has launched a drone delivery pilot in Matthews, North Carolina, offering 20‑minute delivery of select home improvement items through Wing and DoorDash. The pilot covers more than 100 SKUs, ranging from hand tools to paint supplies.
Customers place orders via the DoorDash app, and Wing drones pick up the items from Lowe’s store and fly them to the customer’s location. The service is limited to a curated list of eligible products, including all‑purpose cleaner, caulk, hand tools, household batteries, painter’s tape, screwdrivers and soap. Lowe’s uses its physical stores as hubs for staging drone dispatch areas, integrating DoorDash’s marketplace demand into the drone workflow. The pilot adds to Lowe’s existing same‑day options such as BOPIS, curbside pickup and same‑day delivery.
“By piloting drone delivery, we’re addressing a real project pain point with an innovative solution that is integrated into the retail journey, giving our hometown customers next‑generation fulfillment right when they need it,” Seemantini Godbole, chief information and AI officer at Lowe’s said.
Lowe’s pointed to its AI assistants Mylow and Mylow Companion, which together have answered more than 25 million questions since launching in 2025. The retailer also noted its No. 9 position in the Top 1000 Database and No. 90 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/09/24/lowes-launches-drone-delivery-partnership-wing-doordash)

item.title: FTC seeks comment on impersonation rule update to block platform scam ads
item.description:
The FTC announced today it is considering updating its Impersonation of Government and Businesses Rule after consumers reported nearly $3.5 billion in impersonation fraud losses last year. In 2025, the agency logged more than 1 million imposter‑scam complaints and nearly $3.5 billion in losses, and nearly 30% of victims said they were first approached on social media, where losses totaled $2.1 billion.
The Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, to be published in the Federal Register, asks whether platforms should be required to stop impersonation ads from reaching consumers. It invites comment on how ad‑optimization tools from social media, search engines and other digital marketplaces amplify impersonation scams and whether those tools constitute unfair or deceptive practices. The notice also seeks input on possible regulatory responses, including amending the existing impersonation rule, creating a new rule, or adopting non‑regulatory measures.
“Free markets depend on trust, transparency and consumers’ ability to make informed choices. Impersonation scams—especially when amplified by digital platforms that profit from them—do more than rob Americans of their hard‑earned money,” Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection said.
Impersonation scams have topped the FTC’s fraud‑complaint list in recent years, with the agency logging over 1 million reports and nearly $3.5 billion in losses in 2025. The ANPRM notes that these scams are amplified by search engines, social media and other digital marketplace platforms that profit from optimizing ads for third parties, regardless of the advertisers’ legitimacy.
Source: FTC Press Releases (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/09/ftc-seeks-public-comment-whether-update-rule-impersonation-government-businesses-address-platforms)

item.title: Aldi teams with Deliveroo for online delivery in eight UK stores from October
item.description:
Aldi will trial online grocery delivery with Deliveroo in eight UK stores starting in October A wider rollout across the UK is planned for early 2027
The service will operate under Deliveroo's new Shop & Deliver model, in which riders pick, pack and deliver orders directly from Aldi stores to customers' doors. Shoppers will be able to order a broad selection of Aldi products, including special buys, for same-day delivery via the Deliveroo app. The pilot covers stores in Norwich, Ipswich, Tamworth, Letchworth Garden City and four locations in Kent. For riders, participation in Shop & Deliver is optional and provides an additional earning opportunity outside peak mealtimes.
“We’ve always been committed to bringing low prices to as many people as possible, and this partnership with Deliveroo allows us to do exactly that without changing how our stores operate,” Giles Hurley, chief executive officer at Aldi UK said.
“We are excited to welcome Aldi to the Deliveroo platform through a brand new service, Shop & Deliver. Consumers in several locations across the country will soon be able to enjoy Aldi’s great value and selection delivered to their doorstep on demand,” Rob Harris, VP merchant and chief revenue officer at Deliveroo said.
Aldi had long argued that offering online delivery would hurt its margins and undermine its low-price promise. It halted click-and-collect for special buys and wine in July 2023 and stopped its click-and-collect grocery service in 2024 to keep store operations efficient and prices low.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/aldi-to-offer-online-delivery-through-new-deliveroo-partnership)

item.title: Amazon lets U.S. merchants add free Prime delivery to their sites at no extra cost
item.description:
Amazon now lets U.S. merchants add fast, free Prime delivery to their own websites at no extra cost, with setup 70% faster on average than enabling standalone Buy with Prime. Early adopters have seen over 40% of their eligible orders shipped with Prime delivery.
Merchants can enable the option through the Amazon MCF and Buy with Prime app for Shopify, or via Amazon's Selling Partner API and upcoming integrations with partners like Fulfil, LingXing, and WebBee. When shoppers select Prime delivery at checkout, Amazon verifies their Prime membership and fulfills the order from the merchant's inventory using its logistics network. Order confirmation and tracking are provided directly by the merchant, while the Prime badge appears on product pages to signal the benefit.
“Since enabling it, we've seen a nearly 10% increase in sales, orders go out in about a day and a half, and ‘where is my order?’ inquiries have nearly disappeared,” Gabriella Luksander, general manager at Skinnies Instant Lifts said.
Merchants can turn it on in minutes, with setup 70% faster on average compared to enabling standalone Buy with Prime, and no changes to payments processing, order management, or store policies. Merchants who use Amazon's fulfillment network to ship orders from their own websites can now offer their shoppers something new at checkout: fast, free Prime delivery.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-mcf-prime-delivery-merchant-websites)

item.title: Lidl faces ban on Birkenstock lookalikes in Netherlands after court injunction
item.description:
Lidl faces a €5,000 daily penalty after a Dutch court ordered it to stop selling Birkenstock lookalikes in the Netherlands. The injunction covers Birkenstock’s Arizona, Madrid, Gizeh, Boston and Florida sandal designs.
Lidl must pay €5,000 (about £4,200) for each day it continues to sell the prohibited models. The retailer must also give Birkenstock full details of sales and orders for the affected sandals. Lidl will have to compensate Birkenstock for damages and cover its legal costs, with amounts to be set later. The court said the infringement relates mainly to the distinctive footbed design used across Birkenstock’s footwear.
In November 2025 a Dutch court ordered Scapino to stop selling several Birkenstock lookalikes, a decision that is still under appeal. The Court of Justice of the European Union ruled in December that industrially designed products can qualify for copyright protection when they reflect the creator’s own intellectual creation. Earlier in 2025 Germany’s highest civil court found Birkenstock’s sandals to be functional rather than copyright‑protected works of art.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/lidl-banned-from-selling-birkenstock-lookalikes-after-copyright-ruling)

item.title: Amazon launches always‑on AI agent for third‑party sellers
item.description:
Amazon launched an always‑on AI agent for third‑party sellers on a Wednesday The agent is free for any seller to use and optional, according to Mary Beth Westmoreland, vice president of worldwide selling experience
The always‑on agent can automatically manage pricing, inventory and product performance for merchants. It is built as an upgrade to the Seller Assistant platform, adding new AI‑powered workflows. These workflows run continuously to monitor a seller’s business and respond to changes without manual intervention. As workflows, they can send alerts if a seller’s ratings suddenly decline or monitor pricing for specific products. The platform stores each seller’s profile to generate custom recommendations for item pricing, promotions and inventory management. Through a plug‑in, the agent can connect to external AI tools that sellers already use, initially Amazon’s Quick and Anthropic’s Claude services. The agent is free for any seller to use and optional, as stated by Mary Beth Westmoreland, vice president of worldwide selling experience. Sellers retain control over how much personal data they share with the agent. The new agent expands automation features for easier listing and inventory management. Agents are described as capable of performing multiple actions with little to no human intervention. The always‑on nature means the service runs continuously without requiring sellers to start each action. The platform uses each seller’s profile to tailor workflow recommendations. The agent is free for any seller to use, meaning there is no cost to enable its features.
“The new agent will be free for any seller to use and optional,” Mary Beth Westmoreland, vice president of worldwide selling experience said.
Amazon had previously offered the Seller Assistant platform to assist merchants with listing and inventory management. The upgrade adds AI‑powered workflows that enable continuous, automated actions.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/amazon-launches-always-on-ai-agent-for-marketplace-sellers)

item.title: Sephora starts TikTok Shop with Mikayla Nogueira livestream
item.description:
Sephora launched its TikTok Shop on Saturday with a livestream hosted by Mikayla Nogueira, selling close to 2,300 products so far. The launch featured an exclusive 12‑piece POV Beauty holiday set advertised at a $327 value for $265.
Sephora’s TikTok Shop currently offers only POV Beauty and Sephora Collection items. The retailer plans to add new products on a monthly drop‑model basis. According to NielsenIQ, TikTok Shop is the fourth‑largest health and beauty retailer in the U.S., with sales exceeding $4.4 billion since its 2023 U.S. launch.
“Do these retailers want to go to TikTok Shop? They would prefer that the world comes to their own domain, and they can control that experience. But the world doesn’t really work that way,” Blaine Nielsen, president of retailers at e-commerce agency Rithum said.
Sephora had offered the POV Beauty holiday set since September, with the product page directing shoppers to its newly launched TikTok Shop. In July, Ulta Beauty joined TikTok Shop with a perfume launch featuring Ice Spice.
Source: Modern Retail (https://modernretail.co/marketing/how-sephora-used-mikayla-nogueira-and-pov-beauty-to-kickstart-its-tiktok-shop-launch)

item.title: Amazon expands US pickup network to nearly 30,000 locations
item.description:
Amazon now offers nearly 30,000 pickup locations across the United States. Customers are on track to collect more than 100 million packages from these sites this year. Most U.S. customers have a pickup location within five miles of home.
Shoppers can choose Amazon Lockers, Whole Foods Market stores or other participating sites during checkout. Once a package arrives, Amazon emails a pickup code or barcode with the address and location details.
“We want customers to be able to get their Amazon packages in the way that works best for them,” Viraj Chatterjee, vice president of Amazon Transportation said.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-pickup-locations-expansion)

item.title: Amazon adds persistent memory and Quick-Claude plugin to Seller Assistant
item.description:
Amazon today added persistent memory and a new Quick-Claude plugin to Seller Assistant, which now reaches over 90% of Amazon’s selling partners worldwide. The update also includes a free 12-month Quick Plus subscription for sellers using the new plugin. The assistant retains a long-term record of each seller’s pricing trends, stock cycles, and growth targets, accessible whether they work in Seller Central, Quick or Claude.
Workflows let sellers automate routine tasks such as restocking and price changes, with full audit trails and seller-defined guardrails. The plugin brings Seller Assistant’s AI into Amazon Quick and a beta version of Anthropic’s Claude, allowing sellers to query their business data through natural conversation.
Amazon launched Seller Assistant in 2023 as a generative AI tool to answer questions and surface insights for sellers. After sellers said they wanted more automation, Amazon added agentic capabilities that let the assistant reason, plan, and act on a seller’s behalf.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/seller-assistant-plugin-amazon-quick-claude)

item.title: Amazon, Stella McCartney, and Canopy launch Fashion Coalition with 60+ signatories
item.description:
Today Amazon, Stella McCartney, and Canopy announced the launch of the Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition, which already has over 60 signatories The coalition aims to help its members reach net-zero carbon emissions by 2040
The coalition will align demand across signatories to create blended financing mechanisms that pair development‑finance de‑risking with private capital, helping innovators price sustainable materials closer to mainstream levels. Through its Fashion Coalition Lever Library, members access over 100 proven and emerging options, and fiber‑by‑fiber guidance, while the coalition also uses Next Gen Now, a Canopy‑led initiative, to link signatories with innovative materials ready for commercial adoption. By showing that production‑stage innovations can work at scale, the coalition provides policymakers with real‑world evidence for smarter environmental policy, countering the industry’s estimated 2 to 8% of global carbon emissions, 79 trillion liters of water use, and 92 million tons of annual textile waste. Innovators receive long‑term volume commitments that enable price parity with incumbent fibers, while the coalition’s scaled sustainable materials bring more sustainable fashion choices to customers at every price point
“Through The Climate Pledge, we're bringing together more than 60 fashion and retail brands, manufacturers, and innovators to help make that happen,” Kara Hurst, chief sustainability officer at Amazon said.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/sustainability/amazon-climate-pledge-sustainability-fashion-coalition)

item.title: Amazon explains how 28 years of AWS experience shaped its custom chip designs
item.description:
At the AI Infra Summit on September 16, Amazon senior vice president Peter DeSantis said the company’s 28‑year history with AWS has guided its custom silicon development from Nitro to Graviton to Trainium. He noted that today the vast majority of workloads on AWS run both faster and more cost‑effective on Graviton processors.
The Nitro System moved the virtualization stack onto dedicated hardware, allowing customers to get bare‑metal performance simply by launching an EC2 instance. Graviton processors were developed using internal workload data from Amazon’s own services and customer applications rather than relying on generic benchmarks. Trainium chips were shaped by close work with leading AI customers, and their hardware‑enabled profiler captures fine‑grained telemetry from production workloads without interference. DeSantis highlighted that memory bandwidth often determines how fast a generative model can produce responses, making it a key focus for AI chip design.
“When you're building hardware and building complex systems, understanding the workload deeply is a huge asset,” Peter DeSantis, senior vice president of foundational AI models and custom silicon said.
Amazon now designs chips for networking, general‑purpose computing, and AI, but the company did not set out to become a chip designer. As DeSantis explained, each step in its silicon journey began with a customer workload that needed something better than existing hardware could provide.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/peter-desantis-amazon-ai-chips-design)

item.title: Container shipping on-time performance slips to 29% in August as delays rise
item.description:
Xeneta reported that global container shipping schedule reliability fell for a third straight month in August, with just 29% of vessels arriving on time. The average delay for late vessels rose from 4.2 days in July to 5.1 days in August.
On the Far East–Europe lane, on‑time performance fell ten percentage points to 6% and the average delay reached 8.2 days. Maersk remained the top carrier at 51% on time, despite a six‑point drop, while Hapag‑Lloyd slipped to 46%. Average vessel waiting time in Africa averaged 3.3 days, the highest of any region, ahead of the Middle East at 2.3 days and Southeast Asia at 1.7 days. Ten of the twelve largest carriers recorded lower reliability, narrowing the gap between best and worst performers to 45 percentage points. The Far East–Europe lane continues to contend with the operational effects of the Red Sea crisis, including longer diverted routings around Africa and North European port congestion. In South America’s East Coast trade, average delays doubled to 5.4 days following a three‑day pilotage strike at Argentine ports early in August.
Global container shipping schedule reliability fell for a third consecutive month in August, with just 29% of vessels arriving on time as disruption on the Far East–Europe trade pushed performance close to pandemic-era lows, according to analyst Xeneta. The 4-percentage-point month-to-month decline from July’s 33% on-time performance was accompanied by a sharp increase in the average delay, which rose from 4.2 days to 5.1 days.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/new-report-just-a-third-of-container-shipping-on-time)

item.title: Amazon asks Meta to remove its store from Muse AI agent experience
item.description:
Amazon asked Meta to remove its storefront from the Muse AI agent experience two weeks after the assistant launched and saw Meta’s shares climb 11%. The request follows Meta’s launch of Muse, an AI agent that can shop and pay on behalf of users without identifying itself.
Amazon said it was not given advance notice that Muse would access its online store and did not authorize the agent. The company said Muse does not identify itself when browsing and appears to capture and store shopper credentials. Amazon cited a need for third‑party applications to operate openly and respect retailers’ decisions about participation. The move echoes Amazon’s earlier legal action against Perplexity’s Comet AI agent, which is still pending after a U.S. appeals court overturned a temporary ban in August. Shopify announced it will enable Muse for agentic checkouts across all its stores using Shop Pay.
“We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate,” Lara Hendrickson, Amazon spokesperson said.
In April, Meta signed a deal with Amazon Web Services to use its chips for agentic AI. Amazon has previously blocked Perplexity’s Comet AI agent from accessing its site and is currently litigating that case. Earlier this year Amazon piloted its own “Buy for Me” feature, which lets shoppers buy from external sellers through Amazon’s platform.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/amazon-meta-muse-ai-agent-shopping-experience/831018)

item.title: Gap launches multiyear 'fashiontainment' strategy with boy band Just Your Type
item.description:
Gap has launched a multiyear 'fashiontainment' strategy featuring a partnership with boy band Just Your Type. The partnership notes that Just Your Type has generated more than 450 million views over the past three months. Gap will also roll out a fall capsule collection with the musicians and host fan experiences at malls across the United States.
As part of the deal, Gap will co‑produce a documentary series that offers a look at the band’s live performances, creative process and each of the five members’ personalities. Gap has also developed a fall capsule collection with the musicians and plans to host fan experiences at malls around the United States. The collaboration will include additional social content and activations to support cultural storytelling, using Gap’s brick‑and‑mortar footprint.
“With JYT, we're drawing on the full breadth of Gap — from creative storytelling and fashion to our stores and experiences — to give audiences multiple ways into the band's world,” Pam Kaufman, chief entertainment officer, Gap Inc said.
The news offers an early sign of what to expect from Gap Inc.’s Fashiontainment platform, which it began ramping up this year. The company in January hired former Paramount executive Pam Kaufman as its first chief entertainment officer and has steadily built out the division since. Lourdes Arocho, another Paramount alum, was appointed senior vice president and head of licensing in May while Gap Inc. last month brought on Justin Breton as vice president of development from Walmart.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/gap-rolls-out-fashiontainment-strategy-with-boy-band-collaboration/831023)
